notes: runAuditRecord calls fileFoundAuditRows (found_audit.go:73-76), which returns data unchanged when engine.ReadFoundRequests errors. That function returns nil for a missing store (foundrequest.go:110-112), so an error here is a real read or parse failure. A corrupt found-requests store therefore silently skips the §7 wontfix stamp on rows filed as requests, and the round is graded dirty with no notice. Nothing has been written at this point, so the error could abort the record cleanly. Contrast addFoundOpen, which treats an unreadable queue as an error.

resolved.evidence: 430c02e5 makes fileFoundAuditRows return the ReadFoundRequests error and runAuditRecord exit 3 (cannot read found requests) before any write; 12474390 adds TestFoundAudit_AnUnparsableRequestStoreRefusesTheRecord, green on HEAD and red (exit 0, round file written) with 430c02e5 reverted in a clone

notes: resumeBlockers sets UndecidedRequests from UndecidedRequestIDs, which returns nil when ReadFoundRequests errors (decisionunit.go:30-33). A missing store already reads as empty (foundrequest.go:110-112), so this only hides real read or parse failures. With a corrupt request store, tp resume drops the §5 decision blocker and sends implement work forward silently. The same function's FoundQueueCounts (line 198) propagates its error. Elsewhere: SpecHash at 316 and ClassifyPaths at 145 degrade by design.
